title: Add a camera bar widget that shows when a webcam is in use
head: 450aa80ce104
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Relay instances inheriting CARD_LABEL from the packaged global EnvironmentFile are silently invisible
leads.consequence: The shipped v4l2-relayd@.service first reads /etc/default/v4l2-relayd (CARD_LABEL=Virtual Camera), then optionally reads /etc/v4l2-relayd.d/%i.conf. An active instance with no optional file, or with an instance file that overrides VIDEOSRC but inherits CARD_LABEL, is valid for the service yet skipped by the probe. If its only PipeWire camera source is a loopback, the widget says absent and hides even while that camera is connected and usable. On every next one-second poll it stays absent until its per-instance file explicitly duplicates the global CARD_LABEL.
leads.triage: already covered; Default/inherited CARD_LABEL was R3's third case; now documented as intended by 450aa80 header.

leads.summary: Failed pw-dump fallback counts noncapture and orphan loopback video nodes as webcams
leads.consequence: If pw-dump fails or times out, every existing /dev/videoN counts as a camera without a capture-capability check or active-relay check. An IPU metadata/output-only device makes the icon say idle, or busy if that device is opened, despite no usable webcam. Cam Link's v4l2loopback device persists after the relay and physical capture device stop, so a pw-dump failure then makes its icon reappear even though the successful-pw-dump branch intentionally excludes it. Next polling iteration returns to absent if PipeWire recovers, but persistent failure keeps the wrong state. The new test explicitly expects any device to count in fallback; compare the repository's webcam picker which rejects metadata/output-only nodes.
leads.triage: dropped; pw-dump fallback counting any /dev/videoN is documented in header and accepted in R2; not changed by this commit.

leads.summary: Direct-camera captures owned by unreadable processes never make fuser report busy
leads.consequence: For a direct user of /dev/videoN whose /proc/PID/fd cannot be read by the shell user (different UID or proc restrictions), fuser silently cannot match that FD. The script discards fuser stderr and takes nonzero as no holder; with no PipeWire link it reports idle while another process holds the camera. The widget's record mark is therefore not a cross-account privacy indicator. Restrict the claim to protected processes, not all same-user apps.
leads.triage: dropped; fuser cannot read other users' fds: R3 already noted the root relay case; desktop apps run as the user; outside delta.

leads.summary: Probe failure preserves a prior busy/idle state instead of exposing unknown status
leads.consequence: After a successful busy probe, an abnormal probe with empty/invalid stdout (e.g. mktemp fails, jq unavailable) exits but onExited deliberately ignores that output and keeps cameraState=busy. If the script cannot start at all, shipped Quickshell emits runningChanged but no exited signal, so this handler never runs. The timer retries each second; until a valid probe succeeds it keeps the old record mark or stays hidden if last state was absent, rather than indicating probe failure. The tests only exercise successful busy/idle/absent stdout and script fallback, not QML failure transitions.
leads.triage: corroborated/partly used; QML accepts only three states; used for disabled-state note (Opus confirmed). Stale-on-error aspect not published.

leads.summary: Direct PipeWire v4l2-source nodes can omit api.v4l2.path, disabling direct-open detection
leads.consequence: PipeWire's v4l2-source factory advertises Video/Source and device.api=v4l2 but not api.v4l2.path in its emitted node properties; it defaults the actual device to /dev/video0 when not passed a path. This valid direct-factory source counts toward presence but contributes no fuser path, so an app opening /dev/video0 directly without a PipeWire link leaves the icon idle. Auto-enumerated WirePlumber v4l2 nodes do carry path, so this affects directly created/custom nodes, not the normal monitor path.
leads.triage: dropped; Unusual direct-factory nodes only; hunter qualified it.

leads.summary: Direct PipeWire v4l2-source nodes can omit loopback driver and evade the OBS exclusion
leads.consequence: The probe treats any v4l2 Video/Source lacking the exact api.v4l2.cap.driver="v4l2 loopback" as a real camera. The direct PipeWire v4l2-source producer omits cap.driver; pointing such a source at a loopback /dev/videoN, e.g. an OBS virtual camera, then reports idle despite no active v4l2-relayd instance. This qualifies the new comment's OBS-virtual-camera exclusion, which holds for auto-enumerated nodes carrying driver caps, not direct factory nodes.

leads.summary: #12972 cannot land unchanged next to this widget; preserving the disable switch needs independent USB presence
leads.consequence: The heads diverged and both add the same Camera.qml/Camera.manifest.json and same omarchy.camera ID, plus overlapping docs. Applying #12972's diff to this head fails on both new files and docs. If the proposed USB disable switch is merely grafted onto this PR's probe, disabling a USB camera removes its v4l2 node; this widget's only presence signal becomes absent and hides the button needed to turn it back on. #12972 instead scans USB interfaces for presence and tracks a separate disabled flag, which must be kept if it is rebased here. This is a dependency/integration lead, not a claim that the current PR alone promises a disable switch.
leads.triage: corroborated; #12972 overlap and disabled-state separation; in Opus final; resolved by coordination.

leads.summary: Arch's optional pipewire-libcamera SPA is not in Omarchy's default package lists
leads.consequence: The new libcamera Video/Source branch detects an existing PipeWire node, but Arch packages the SPA libcamera plugin separately as pipewire-libcamera, an optdepend of pipewire. Neither the default package lists nor the shipped intel-ipu7-camera recipe installs it. A machine relying on native libcamera rather than the stock IPU7 v4l2loopback relay has no such PipeWire source on the default package set; if pw-dump itself succeeds and there are no other webcams, the widget remains absent. This is conditional on a native libcamera-only camera; IPU7's package explicitly uses the relay instead, so no claim is made that stock IPU7 is broken.
leads.triage: dropped; Generic QML integration test request; not demonstrated benefit.

leads.summary: Camera QML integration has no assertion that the probe starts or updates visibility
leads.consequence: A plausible mutant that sets Camera.qml's Timer.running=false or deletes onExited while retaining the shell probe passes the camera-widget-test.sh probe fixtures, the final negative grep and clone check. The bar-widget-contract and manifest tests only load/instantiate the QML, not drive it through an idle-to-busy transition. Add a QML integration assertion that feeds a stub busy/idle/absent probe and checks visible and active state; the existing shell tests cannot catch a permanently absent indicator. Weak-test issue, lower priority than the runtime failures.
leads.triage: dropped; Native libcamera package absence is pre-existing and outside the follow-up delta.

limits: Current quattro base tip 3faafba manual merge clean; no assigned compositor slot, so QML runtime contract tests were source-read, not executed.

The direct-v4l2 omissions H5/H5b require direct factory nodes rather than WirePlumber's normal enumeration; producer source and synthetic probe fixture confirm possibility, not prevalence on typical users.
A failed or unknown process exit is masked in QML H4; real-world frequency of mktemp failure is not measured.

flags.disposition: real error, fixed; Narrowed to MIPI cameras (IPU7 relay, MIPI libcamera source); Cam Link relay and USB libcamera sources do go away.

flags.disposition: real error, fixed; Added 'If those were the only cameras' and reworded heading.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13019#issuecomment-5855259343) of `e8e6eff` and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13019#issuecomment-5855336888), checked against `450aa80`.

**Verified:** `450aa80` changes only the header comment of `camera-busy.sh`. With comment lines removed, the probe is identical to `e8e6eff`. The camera, clone and plugin tests pass on the new head. The new header text matches the code.

| Earlier point | Status on `450aa80` |
|---|---|
| Loopbacks without a matching active relay no longer count | Resolved. The exclusion is intended, and the [`camera-busy.sh` header](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/450aa80ce1048a331c28775d02df88c8ec3c0a80/shell/plugins/bar/widgets/camera-busy.sh#L18-L20) now states it, covering the OBS, instance-name and `CARD_LABEL` cases. |
| Overlapping open PR #12972 | Resolved by coordination. #12972 becomes the switch on top of this PR and stays a draft until this one lands. For that rebase: #12972 also edits the same Camera row and paragraph in `manual/05-the-top-bar.md` and the same row in `shell/plugins/bar/README.md`, so those conflict too, not only the widget files. |
| Stopped relay never exercised by the test | Still open (optional, below) |
| Polling cost | Unchanged, still unmeasured |
| Cam Link loopback, hung-`pw-dump` timing, clone, device scope, `pw-dump` timeout, test stubs, enable command, manual table | Resolved earlier. The probe code is unchanged, and the tests still pass. |

**Optional test improvement:** the stopped-relay case from the previous review still applies, now at [`camera-widget-test.sh#L365-L368`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/450aa80ce1048a331c28775d02df88c8ec3c0a80/test/shell.d/camera-widget-test.sh#L365-L368) and [`camera-busy.sh#L149`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/450aa80ce1048a331c28775d02df88c8ec3c0a80/shell/plugins/bar/widgets/camera-busy.sh#L149). With that line's `|| continue` changed to `|| true`, the test still passes. Appending the suggested case (`add_relay camlink "Cam Link 4K" /dev/video2`, then `: >"$tmp/active-relays"`, then `PROBE_KEEP_RELAYS=1 probe "$tmp/loopback.json"` expecting `absent`) passes on this head and fails on that altered copy with `idle`. The PR description still lists "a loopback source left after unplug" as covered, but that case runs with no relay config at all.

### Notes on the proposed `disabled` state

These bear on the [discussion about #12972](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13019#issuecomment-5861230148), not on a defect in this PR. They are traced in source and in probe runs with synthetic data, not on hardware.

- **The current head does report `absent` with cameras off.** #12972's switch deauthorizes the USB video interfaces. The kernel then unbinds `uvcvideo` and removes the `/dev/videoN` node, and PipeWire drops the node. If those were the only cameras, the probe prints `absent`, and [`Camera.qml`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/450aa80ce1048a331c28775d02df88c8ec3c0a80/shell/plugins/bar/widgets/Camera.qml#L13-L16) hides the widget (`visible: present`).
- **A fourth state needs QML changes too.** [`Camera.qml#L45-L49`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/450aa80ce1048a331c28775d02df88c8ec3c0a80/shell/plugins/bar/widgets/Camera.qml#L45-L49) accepts only `busy`, `idle` and `absent`, and ignores any other output. A probe that prints `disabled` alone would leave the widget in its previous state. `present`, the icon and the tooltip need to handle it as well.
- **Let `busy` take precedence over `disabled`.** The probe also counts cameras the USB switch does not turn off, such as MIPI cameras: the IPU7 camera that the `intel-ipu7-camera` package relays through `v4l2-relayd@ipu7`, or a MIPI camera exposed as a libcamera source. On a laptop with that camera plus a USB webcam, a `disabled` state that overrides the probe could show "disabled" while an app is using the IPU7 camera. Showing `disabled` only when no non-USB camera counts would also avoid this.

**Optional:** in the idle state the tooltip reads "Camera live" ([`Camera.qml#L58`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/450aa80ce1048a331c28775d02df88c8ec3c0a80/shell/plugins/bar/widgets/Camera.qml#L58)), which can read as "in use". #12972 uses "Camera ready".

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Follow-up source review of `450aa80` against `e8e6eff`, with #12972 at `5bf34df`, Linux 7.2 USB and UVC sources, PipeWire 1.6.9, v4l2loopback 0.15.4 and the `intel-ipu7-camera` package. Sandboxed runs of the PR's camera, clone and plugin tests, an altered copy of the probe and an extended copy of the test, and the probe with synthetic `pw-dump`, relay and sysfs data. Not tested: webcam, Cam Link or IPU7 hardware, a live PipeWire, udev or systemd session, the rendered widget, and per-tick CPU cost.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
